name: TMA Soak Tests
objective: Exercise all the systems available using the Scheduler to simulate operations for as long as possible.
precondition: Ideally, we want to run this test with as many components as possible. However, there are many situations where one or more subsystems are unavailable. At least two components should be available to run this test. The different combinations are represented as different steps.

name: Top-End Assembly Vibration Investigation using BLOCK-197
objective: Understand better what is the source of the vibration on the Top-End Assembly
precondition:
The telescope should be at Zenith and both hexapods enable.
This blocks uses the Rotator as well and the laser tracker.

Not on sky, no tma movement.

name: BLOCK-259 - Generation of Coordinate Transformation Matrix between Laser Tracker and Hexapod Coord Systems
objective:
Use BLOCK-259 - Generation of Coordinate Transformation Matrix between Laser Tracker and Hexapod Coord. Systems.
This BLOCK is now split into four parts.
  • BLOCK-259_1 moves the Camera Hexapod in X, Y, and Z and takes measurements
  • BLOCK-259_2 moves the Camera Hexapod in U and V and takes measurements
  • BLOCK-259_3 moves the M2 Hexapod in X, Y, and Z and takes measurements
  • BLOCK-259_4 moves the M2 Hexapod in U and V and takes measurements

This test case is designed to consider the three parts above and it considers configurations where we have the MTRotator enabled or in standby.
Subsets of data are acceptable depending on the goal of the study. 
For example, we can run BLOCK-259_1 twice one day and BLOCK-259_2 twice in the following day.
But each pair should be taken within a single day.
The block parts that move x, y and z should be executed first.
precondition:
These blocks require the hexapods to be in compensation mode. And can only be enabled when the telescope is below 90º.
So we need to take the telescope out of the parking position before executing this test case.

name: TMA Tracking jitter on sky using the Fast Camera
objective:
This test case is an alias for BLOCK-217 - TMA Tracking jitter on sky - fast video.
The idea is to take videos to check the tracking jitter.
precondition: See the BLOCK-217 description for details in the pre-conditions.

Elevation Sweep Laser Tracker Measurements of M2 and Camera with the Yellow Cross
objective: Evaluate the gravity Look-Up Table for M2 and Camera Hexapods using the Laser Tracker for measuring their position at different elevation angles.
precondition:

  • MTPtg

  • MTHexapod:2

  • LaserTracker

name: BLOCK-202 - AOS Single Loop using Hexapods and Comcam
objective:
The goal of this test case is to ingest a simulated image using the playback mode of ComCam.
This means that even though simulated, the system after the DAQ behaves as if it were real.
This includes the DM pipeline (Butler, OCPS, etc) and, in a later stage, the AOS correction loop.
In this particular test case, we are focusing on the Active Optics pipeline.

Demonstrate:
• Slew to an observing field, generating telemetry (cf. IMF)
• piston the camera in Z-direction (e.g. in, -out, in, +out, in).
• take data using ComCam in playback mode, commanded from the OCS
• uses OCPS to reduce the data on the commissioning cluster
• load the Zernike coefficients into the EFD
• Use the MTAOS to update the state of the optics

Associated Documents
  • Document-14771 - Active Optics Baseline Design
  • LSE-186 - Main Telescope Active Optics System: Wavefront Estimation Pipeline and Optical Feedback Controller Requirement Document

This is almost the same as LVV-T2228.
But, here, we use BLOCKs.
precondition:
You will need:
  • MTHexapod:1
  • MTHexapod:2
  • CCCamera in playback mode
  • CCOODS
  • CCHeaderService
  • MTAOS
  • MTMount (can be simulated)
  • MTRotator (can be simulated)

name: BLOCK-262 - Measure residual forces on M2 to verify Look-Up Table

precondition:

M2 needs to be in closed loop.

name: OR4 Night 1
objective:
The objective of this test is to run the OR4 SV sub-data blocks throughout the night.  Each sub-block takes about 40 minutes to run and typically has 60 (or sometimes 120) exposures as it follows a field on the sky.  The goal is to match when these run to the local time.  It may be necessary to skip some sub-blocks as they take somewhat longer to actually run than calculated. Also, these are expected to be run after the AOS tests.  So, one should start at the nearest to local time.

As you are running, you can check the Simulated ComCam RubinTV page to make sure data is flowing properly. You can also check the ComCam CCS viewer.
precondition:
Make sure that the OCS queue is enabled along with the OCS scheduler. On the Summary State view, the OCS queue and scheduler are labeled as ScriptQueue3 and Scheduler3.

You also need to make sure that the CCCamera, CCODS, and CCHeaderService and enabled. If it still necessary after previous setups, you can use the maintel/enable_comcam.py script to enable the components. The CCCamera should be in simulation mode. It is not currently possible to check this with LOVE so, consult a commissioning scientist if this is not the case or you are unclear on the status of the components.

For each step below you will run a sub-block using the OCS queue along with the OCS scheduler.

For each sub-block, using osc/scheduler/add_block.py in the OCS queue with the following yaml config. Replace the id line with that in the step of test. Mark each step as completed, skipped etc. You can compare the time of the step completion with the start time of the next step.

id: ops-rehearsal-4-{Sub-block}

name: ASCT-001 Manual Alignment
objective:
Perform initial manual alignment of the SST optics using both mirrors, hexapods and ComCam.
The process is mostly manual and the steps in the Test Script might be followed in any order depending on the state of the system.
This test requires a test scientist driving the changes.

In summary, we want to move hexapods to tweak the image quality by eye, on axis, and over the full FoV.

Analysis
  • Eye-balling the correct alignment. See PSF are sharper.
  • Analysis is quick, use the brightest thing in each sensor, to not rely on ISR.
  • Use RubinTv plots and printouts for diagnosis. 

Failure Mitigation
Continue the alignment for a couple of iterations and then move to the next test.

Success Criteria
We are in-focus enough to start with a focus sweep.
precondition:
We want all components available (Dome, Simonyi Telescope, M1M3, M2, Hexapods, ComCam).
The optics must be roughly aligned with the Laser Tracker.

This test requires on sky data.
Find a very bright star and take 2 s (very short) exposure to be able to react "faster".

name: TMA Fine Balance
objective:
We want to find the position in Z and in Y of the counterweights located inside the Telescope Mount Assembly that minimizes the torques in the elevation axis.
The test itself consists into moving the telescope to Zenith/Horizon and find the best position for these counterweights in Z/Y.
We might need multiple interactions up/down.

For the sake of traceability, please:
  • Write down the name of the Setting Set used to configure the TMA when executing this test into the first step Actual Results.
  • Record any time we move the counterweights and their final position.
    It seems they are recorded in the EFD but it is easier to have them in OLE to have a narrative.
  • Add the hardware configuration in the execution comments field. Examples are:
    TMA Balance with ComCam + M2 or TMA Balance with ComCam + M2 + M1M3
precondition:
The critical components that must be running and in ENABLED state are:
  • M1M3 - Running in closed loop - if installed.
  • M2 - Running in closed loop - if installed.

For the TMA, confirm via EUI that:
  • Power Supply is On
  • Oil Supply System is up and running
  • Locking Pins are in a LOCK position
  • The telescope should be roughly balanced - this means that the torque values in the elevation drives should be within the safe range of +/- 2500 N.

name: Workout Camera Hexapod
objective:
We want to understand how high the temperatures in the camera hexapod legs and nearby increase as we move them in and out of focus. This is very similar to the warm-up test cases, but we want to exercise moving the hexapod in and out of focus for two hours (very similar to how comcam will operate during the first weeks of AOS testing, to take multiple triplets - i.e., intra/extra/in-focus sequences).

 

There are a few points to take into consideration:
  • Safety Issue:  The temperature in all the hexapods legs (struts) should be less than 30 ºC. The hexapods were designed with a low operational  temperature range -3 to 19 C. However, they should operate safely up to 30 ºC. Anything above 40 ºC will be very bad as the lubricant used, SKF LGBB2,  begins separating at that temperature and could contaminate the encoder tape.
  • Image Quality Issue: The temperature difference between the camera hexapod and the ambient temperature should be less than +1 ºC / -2 ºC. We should use ESS:1 to monitor these temperatures. This is relevant for posterior analysis.

Visualization:
- Monitor the following dashboard

Execution Time:
This Test Case is configured to use the Scheduler CSC to run the block (BLOCK-T81). It will continue to queue up the scripts until the scheduler is stopped. Ideally, we would run it for about 2hrs, but it can be shorter or longer depending on needs.
precondition:

name: ASCT-002 Focus Sweep and Alignment Camera Hexapod
objective:
Test Objective:
The aim of this test is to conduct a focus sweep on the telescope by individually adjusting one degree of freedom (x, y, z, rx, ry) of the Camera hexapod. This process involves systematically offsetting each parameter and moving through the focus range. Throughout the iterations, we will plot the Point Spread Function (PSF) to identify the optimal focus point and apply the necessary corrections.

Key Considerations:
  1. Optimal Positioning: The "optimal position" for each degree of freedom adjustment must fall within the range of offsets applied during the test series. 
  2. Offset Magnitude: The offsets should be small enough to ensure that the sources can still be approximated by a PSF, avoiding shapes like donuts or high aberration conditions.

Success Criteria:
  • Maximum PSF intensity.
  • Minimum PSF Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM).
  • The PSF shape is as circular (round) as possible.

Mitigation Strategies:
  • If the PSF is not seeing-limited, verify the telescope's pointing accuracy and repeat the test. This step requires the Differential Image Motion Monitor (DIMM) to be operational.
precondition:
Optics should in a good enough state that the sources can be well described by Point Spread Function (PSF).
System is pre-aligned with laser tracker.

name: ASCT-002 Focus Sweep and Alignment M2 Hexapod
objective:
Test Objective:
The aim of this test is to conduct a focus sweep on the telescope by individually adjusting one degree of freedom (x, y, z, rx, ry) of the M2 hexapod. This process involves systematically offsetting each parameter and moving through the focus range. Throughout the iterations, we will plot the Point Spread Function (PSF) to identify the optimal focus point and apply the necessary corrections.

Key Considerations:
  1. Optimal Positioning: The "optimal position" for each degree of freedom adjustment must fall within the range of offsets applied during the test series. 
  2. Offset Magnitude: The offsets should be small enough to ensure that the sources can still be approximated by a PSF, avoiding shapes like donuts or high aberration conditions

Success Criteria:
  • Maximum PSF intensity.
  • Minimum PSF Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM).
  • The PSF shape is as circular (round) as possible.

Mitigation Strategies:
  • If the PSF is not seeing-limited, verify the telescope's pointing accuracy and repeat the test. This step requires the Differential Image Motion Monitor (DIMM) to be operational.
precondition:
Optics should in a good enough state that the sources can be well described by Point Spread Function (PSF).
System is pre-aligned with laser tracker.

name: WET-001 Optical State Hexapods
objective:
Test goal:
The objective of this test is to validate the system's ability to estimate its optical state when constrained to hexapod degrees of freedom (DoF). This will be accomplished by applying different hexapod degrees of freedom and evaluating the system's response.

The sequence applied is
- M2 dz
- Cam dx
- M2 rx
- Cam ry
- M2 rx, Cam dz, M2 dx (a combination of degrees of freedom)

Before the test, a sensitivity matrix for the selected hexapod DoF must be generated. Alternatively, the test can proceed using a sensitivity matrix derived from simulation data.

This test will be repeated across various combinations of hexapod DoF and observation conditions to ensure the Active Optics System (AOS) meets performance requirements under different scenarios. After it has been run with steps the first time, a JSON block will probably be created.

Monitoring:
- Check the evolution of degrees of freedom from Chronograph
- Check the optical state estimates in Chronograph
- Check the wavefront estimation results

Note: This test case is specifically focused on hexapod DoF. Other test cases in the suite will involve additional degrees of freedom.
precondition:
- Telescope aligned with laser tracker
- Telescope focused
- Wavefront estimation validated and sensitivity matrix built

name: ASCT-009 Dome Slit Coordinate System
objective: The goal of this test is to disentangle the coordinate systems. We will point the telescope at the center/edge of the dome slit and see how the donuts are or are not vignetted in the images. We will do that by slowly moving the telescope in Azimuth in one direction and then the other. The goal is to understand what is the direction of +/- azimuthal rotation in the image plane. To do this we will have to stop the dome, so the dome does not follow the TMA. It is important to make sure we are only taking intra-focal images (-1500 um).
precondition:
Telescope pre-aligned with laser tracker
Manual alignment performed until images are focused enough to be described by a PSF (and then the camera is defocus to be intrafocal).

name: ASCT-010 Mirror Cover Coordinate System
objective: The goal of this test is to disentangle coordinate systems. We will deploy particular M1M3 mirror covers at known pupil coordinates and take an intrafocal image to establish the relation between pupil and image planes. We will then rotate the camera and watch how that affects the images, to understand what is the direction of camera rotation. It is important to make sure we are only taking intra-focal images (-1500 um).

Telescope pre-aligned with laser tracker
Manual alignment performed until stars are focused enough that they can be described by a PSF

name: Simonyi ComCam Feature Based Scheduler Flexible Science Verification Survey
objective:
The objective of this test is to collect sequences of ComCam images for science pipelines commissioning.

The observations are implemented with the Feature Based Scheduler to allow running this test at any time that the system can achieve acceptable image quality for science pipelines testing (e.g., PSF FWHM < 2 arcsec).

This test case is intended to be run as part of a multi-night observing campaign, i.e., this test could be repeated on multiple nights.

The underlying scheduler configuration is expected to be updated to adjust the prioritization of target fields, constraints, dither pattern, exposure time, band selection, etc., based on the evolving system capabilities as we move through on-sky commissioning w/ ComCam.

The data will be used for multiple science pipeline commissioning tasks, including:
  • Solving and validating the camera distortion model, including tests of astrometric repeatability
  • Solving and validating the illumination correction, including tests of photometric repeatability
  • Test building deep coadds
  • Test building templates for difference imaging and running difference image analysis

Note: Goal to accumulate epochs on many nights for routine testing of Prompt Processing and DIA in as many bands as possible
  • For example, 10 visits in each of the three loaded filters per epoch
  • General preference to observe in 3 bands per epoch, to enable as many different tests as possible
precondition:
Telescope tracking + optically focused and aligned for 30 second visits, w/ acceptable delivered image quality across the ComCam field of view.

Confidence that the system can maintain the performance above for at least 30 min to 1 hour, including focal plane scale dithers between visits and larger slews between fields.

This Test Case uses a configurable BLOCK to validate the wavefront estimation pipeline (WEP) using different color targets at high airmass in order to observe how the WEP handles atmospheric chromaticity. This BLOCK is part of the ComCam AOS tests. Analysis will be done offline. This BLOCK will enable ComCam, slew to a configurable RA/Dec, and take two triplets at a configurable exposure time.

The test case is broken up into three steps to ease execution. This BLOCK is designed to run on whatever filter is already installed on ComCam. If possible, it should be run in more than one filter, but this would not need to be done consecutively.

Observing Condition Requirements:
This BLOCK should be run near the horizon in clear weather at three separate airmasses (zenith angles).

While running this block:
  • check the images of the donuts : RubinTV
precondition:
Telescope is focused.
ComCam ​enabled.
​High airmass target.

name: Apply Bending Mode to M1M3/M2
objective: This test applies a bending mode to M1M3/M2 using the apply_dof.py script, which sends forces to the actuators. When executed, it will mark the first time a bending mode has been applied to M1M3/M2 since the mirror left the Mirror Lab. This test is essential for validating the interface between subsystems, as the script leverages the same functions that MTAOS uses to apply corrections to the mirror, providing a critical assessment of the system's overall integration and functionality.
precondition: M1M3 is raised and actuators are working.

name: Minimum Functionality Test Following Long Rotator Shutdown
objective:
Objective:
Verify the rotator can operate smoothly across its full range of motion without oscillations or overcurrent issues, ensuring the system's stability and performance under various movement conditions.

Description:
This test will assess the rotator's ability to perform controlled movements within its operational limits. The sequence includes incremental movements:
  1. Perform 2 or 3 small movements in both directions (±1 degrees).
  2. Execute 2 or 3 somewhat medium movements (±5-10 degrees).
  3. Move the rotator to its maximum limits (±89.8 degrees).

Additional Notes:
  1. Tekniker has recently updated the controller filters to mitigate overcurrent issues. During this test, we will monitor current levels to ensure that these improvements effectively prevent overcurrent conditions.
  2. The rotator's current default configuration parameters are as follows (those can be monitored in the MTRotator chronograf dashboard):
    • Velocity (v) = 3.5
    • Acceleration (a) = 1.0
    • Jerk (j) = 4.0

Ensure all movements are monitored for any signs of oscillation (vms) or overcurrent (chronograf dashboard) to confirm the system operates within safe parameters. Since Tekniker updated PID loop, watch also torque and position in choronograf.
precondition:
MTRotator startup procedure was completed without issues:
  • MTRotator is ENABLED
  • MTMount is ENABLED
Hexapods are ON
M2 and Rotator VMSs are ON 

Note 1: Rotator current should exceed 3.5 A.
Note 2: Monitor oscillations.
Note 3: Note that we are using mtmount_ccw_only version. Confirm with a Comm-Sci this is true.

name: AuxTel New LUT Test
objective: This test evaluates the performance of the new LUT on the Auxiliary Telescope (AuxTel) at different elevations to ensure the applied corrections are accurate and reasonable, and that the telescope's pointing remains stable. The test involves both day and night activities: during the day, we begin by checking the LUT's behavior at different elevations, followed by night operations where corrections are applied at under real observing conditions and the pointing is checked. This ensures the quality of future data and telescope performance. After some weeks of operations, an offline analysis will be required to confirm that the LUT correctly captured all temperature dependencies and that the closed-loop offsets are now centered around zero, indicating that the system is properly calibrated.

name: AuxTel Optical Alignment Check
objective:
This test evaluates the pointing and alignment of the AuxTel following the collision with the limit switch on September 26th. The goal is to run a set of standard scripts (correct_pointing and wep_align) at a few different positions and perform some rough, by-eye checks of the pointing accuracy and optical alignment. 


If the optics of the telescope experienced a significant shift, the first images will very likely be either poorly centered, very poor image quality (e.g triangular point sources) or a combination of both. If the optics are near to there nominal positions, we expect both scripts to succeed at all positions.
precondition: Before running this test, you should run the atpneumatics_checkout.py script three times to ensure the primary mirror is settled into position. This can be done during the daytime.

name: WET-001 Optical State M2 Bending
objective:
Test goal:
The objective of this test is to validate the system's ability to estimate its optical state when constrained to M2 bending mode degrees of freedom (DoF). This will be accomplished by applying different M2 bending degrees of freedom and evaluating the system's response.

The sequence applied is
- M2 B1
- M2 B2
- M2 B3
- M2 B5
- M2 B4, M2 B6, M2 B8 (combination of bending modes)

Before the test, a sensitivity matrix for the selected M2 bending DoF must be generated. Alternatively, the test can proceed using a sensitivity matrix derived from simulation data.

This test will be repeated across various combinations of DoF and observation conditions to ensure the Active Optics System (AOS) meets performance requirements under different scenarios. After it has been run with steps the first time, a JSON block will probably be created.

Monitoring:
- Check the evolution of degrees of freedom from Chronograph
- Check the optical state estimates in Chronograph
- Check the wavefront estimation results

Note: This test case is specifically focused on M2 bending DoF. Other test cases in the suite will involve additional degrees of freedom.
precondition:
- Telescope aligned with laser tracker
- Telescope focused
- Wavefront estimation validated and sensitivity matrix built

name: WET-001 Optical State Characteristic Modes

The sequence applied is

- M1M3 B2, M2 B1
- M2 ​dz, Cam dz, M1M3 B3, M2 B5
- M1M3 B4, M2 B3

Before the test, a sensitivity matrix for all the degrees of freedom must be generated. Alternatively, the test can proceed using a sensitivity matrix derived from simulation data.

This test will be repeated across various combinations of DoF and observation conditions to ensure the Active Optics System (AOS) meets performance requirements under different scenarios. After it has been run with steps the first time, a JSON block will probably be created.

Monitoring:
- Check the evolution of degrees of freedom from Chronograph
- Check the optical state estimates in Chronograph
- Check the wavefront estimation results

Note: This test case is specifically focused on combinations of DoF to probe as well the degeneracy of the system. Other test cases in the suite involve individual subsets of degrees of freedom.
precondition:
- Telescope aligned with laser tracker
- Telescope focused
- Wavefront estimation validated and sensitivity matrix built

name: Top end thermal tests: Soak Test w/ Camera Hexapod with DISABLED state between targets
objective:
This test aims to evaluate the thermal impact of actuating the Camera Hexapod (MTHexapod:1) while mitigating heating effects by disabling it between simulated slews. Specifically, it focuses on Test 5 outlined in SITCOM-1631 (Top end thermal tests), which involves disabling the camera hexapod for 32 seconds between movements and keep all other top end components off (with exception of M2).

The goal is to assess the effectiveness of this operational mitigation in reducing temperature buildup and its influence on dome seeing and image quality. The test simulates real observation conditions over an extended period (ideally 8 hours) to account for the thermal time constants of the system, which are expected to be several hours. The focus is on measuring any temperature increases and evaluating the mitigation strategy's effectiveness in minimizing thermal gradients that could adversely affect image quality due to dome seeing.

Note that the test is basically ignoring MTMount, MTRotator, MTHexapod:2, MTAOS, MTM1M3, MTDome and MTDomeTrajectory.
precondition:
• The MTRotator, MTHexapod:1 and MTHexapod:2 must have been powered off for at least 8 hours before starting the test to ensure thermal stabilization.
  • The MTRotator and MTHexapod:2 will remain powered off for the duration of the test.
  • The MTMount CSC can be running in any mode since it will be ignored.
  • Camera Hexapod compensation mode should be disabled.
  • Keep the following components ENABLED:
    • MTHexapod:1 (Camera Hexapod)

      Note: M2 remains in closed loop all the time.

name: Top end thermal tests: Soak Test w/ Camera Hexapod with ENABLED state between targets
objective:
This test aims to evaluate the thermal impact of continuously actuating the Camera Hexapod (MTHexapod:1) without mitigation. Specifically, it focuses on Test 3 outlined in SITCOM-1631 (Top End Thermal Tests), where the camera hexapod drives remain enabled for the duration of the test, unlike Test 5 where the hexapod was disabled between slews. It evaluates the thermal effects of continuous actuation of the Camera Hexapod (MTHexapod:1) over a prolonged period, without powering it off between slews. The thermal impact will be monitored using temperature sensors on the camera hexapod, focusing on the shrouded area to detect any significant increases in temperature.

The goal is to assess how continuous actuation impacts temperature buildup in the shrouded area surrounding the Camera Hexapod and its effect on dome seeing and image quality. This test will simulate real observation conditions, running for an extended period (ideally 8 hours) to account for the system's thermal time constants. The test will help determine if the Camera Hexapod’s actuation alone, without operational mitigation, contributes significantly to top-end heating and potential beam deflection issues.

Note that the test is basically ignoring MTMount, MTRotator, MTHexapod:2, MTAOS, MTM1M3, MTDome and MTDomeTrajectory.
precondition:
• The MTRotator, MTHexapod:1 and MTHexapod:2 must have been powered off for at least 8 hours before starting the test to ensure thermal stabilization.
  • The MTRotator and MTHexapod:2 will remain powered off for the duration of the test.
  • The MTMount CSC can be running in any mode since it will be ignored.
  • Camera Hexapod compensation mode should be disabled.
  • Keep the following components ENABLED:
    • MTHexapod:1 (Camera Hexapod)

      Note: M2 remains in closed loop all the time.

name: TMA Coarse Balance
objective:
We want to find a configuration of counterweights required to balance the Telescope Mount Assembly considering different hardware configurations.
The test itself consists into moving the telescope up and down at a very low velocity to prevent damage to the mirrors.
Every time the telescope reaches an end, we review the data and add/remove counterweights as needed.

For the sake of traceability, please:
  • Write down the name of the Setting Set used to configure the TMA when executing this test into the first step Actual Results.
  • Record any time we install/remove counterweights on the TMA in OLE.
    We want to include the weights and their location (M1M3 Cell +X -Y or TEA -X - Y, for example).
  • Add the hardware configuration in the execution comments field. Examples are:
    TMA Balance with ComCam + M2 or TMA Balance with ComCam + M2 + M1M3
precondition:
The critical components that must be running and in ENABLED state are:
  • If installed, M1M3 - It should be running in closed loop and the Slew Flag should be active. The Slew Flag will enable the Inertia Compensation System (ICS) and open the booster valves in the force actuators. 
  • If installed, M2 - It should be running in closed loop.

For the TMA, confirm via EUI that:
  • Power Supply is On
  • Oil Supply System is up and running
  • Locking Pins are in a LOCK position

Safety - This work is likely to happen on Level 8 with a few people in the Azimuth Platform.
Ensure to have a Mechanical Engineer following the procedure.
Ensure to have someone ready to press an E-Stop button for a quick response in case of any incident.

name: Top end thermal tests: Soak Test w/ M2 Hexapod with ENABLED state between targets
objective:
This test aims to evaluate the thermal impact of continuously actuating the M2 Hexapod (MTHexapod:1) without mitigation. Specifically, it focuses on Test 2 outlined in SITCOM-1631 (Top End Thermal Tests), where the m2 hexapod drives remain enabled for the duration of the test, unlike Test 4 where the hexapod was disabled between slews. It evaluates the thermal effects of continuous actuation of the M2 Hexapod (MTHexapod:2) over a prolonged period, without powering it off between slews. The thermal impact will be monitored using temperature sensors on the camera hexapod, focusing on the shrouded area to detect any significant increases in temperature.

The goal is to assess how continuous actuation impacts temperature buildup in the shrouded area surrounding the Camera Hexapod and its effect on dome seeing and image quality. This test will simulate real observation conditions, running for an extended period (ideally 8 hours) to account for the system's thermal time constants. The test will help determine if the Camera Hexapod’s actuation alone, without operational mitigation, contributes significantly to top-end heating and potential beam deflection issues.

Note that the test is basically ignoring MTMount, MTRotator, MTHexapod:1, MTAOS, MTM1M3, MTDome and MTDomeTrajectory.
precondition:
• The MTRotator, MTHexapod:1 and MTHexapod:2 must have been powered off for at least 8 hours before starting the test to ensure thermal stabilization.
  • The MTRotator and MTHexapod:1 will remain powered off for the duration of the test.
  • The MTMount CSC can be running in any mode since it will be ignored.
  • Camera Hexapod compensation mode should be disabled.
  • Keep the following components ENABLED:
    • MTHexapod:2 (M2 Hexapod)

      Note: M2 remains in closed loop all the time.

name: ASCT-002 Alignment Sweep Camera Hexapod (parameter march)
objective:
Test Objective:
The aim of this test is to conduct a focus sweep on the telescope by individually adjusting one degree of freedom (x, y, z, rx, ry) of the Camera hexapod. This process involves systematically offsetting each parameter and moving through the focus range. Throughout the iterations, we will plot the Point Spread Function (PSF) to identify the optimal focus point and apply the necessary corrections.

Key Considerations:
  1. Optimal Positioning: The "optimal position" for each degree of freedom adjustment must fall within the range of offsets applied during the test series. 
  2. Offset Magnitude: The offsets should be small enough to ensure that the sources can still be approximated by a PSF, avoiding shapes like donuts or high aberration conditions.

Success Criteria:
  • Maximum PSF intensity.
  • Minimum PSF Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM).
  • The PSF shape is as circular (round) as possible.

Mitigation Strategies:
  • If the PSF is not seeing-limited, verify the telescope's pointing accuracy and repeat the test. This step requires the Differential Image Motion Monitor (DIMM) to be operational.
precondition:
Optics should in a good enough state that the sources can be well described by Point Spread Function (PSF).

name: Closed-dome Light Leak Checks - Nighttime
objective:
Collect a series of exposures with the Dome Closed to assess conditions for calibrations. We would like to simulate the position used for aligning the telescope with the calibrations screen, which will be mounted on the Dome. 

This test consists of:
  • Ensuring the dome shutter is closed
  • Ensuring there are no visible lights on the in the dome (e.g. dark conditions).
  • Recording the current azimuth position of the Dome, to be used to calculate the input position for the telescope
  • Running a JSON BLOCK, which will execute the following steps
    • Disable Dome following
    • Slew the telescope to the calibration screen position (+95.3 deg away from dome azimuth position)
    • Collect a series of 5x30s ENGTEST images with the shutter open to measure ambient light conditions
    • Repeat this block for all filters currently installed in ComCam.
precondition: Dome is closed and observations are unavailable due to weather conditions.

name: Closed-dome Light Leak Checks - Daytime
objective:
Collected a series of exposures with the telescope and dome in the calibration screen position using a set of different dome azimuth angles to assess the best position for afternoon/morning calibrations. 

This test consists of the following steps:
  • Ensuring the dome shutter is closed
  • Ensuring there are no visible lights on the in the dome (e.g. dark conditions).
  • Recording the current azimuth position of the Dome, to be used to calculate the input position for the telescope
  • Disabling dome following
  • Positioning the telescope at the calibration screen position (+95.3 deg away from current dome azimuth position)
  • Running a set of test exposures to ensure saturation levels will not be reached when running the data collection JSON BLOCK
  • Running a JSON BLOCK, which will execute the following steps
    • Disable Dome following
    • Slew the telescope to the calibration screen position (+95.3 deg away from dome azimuth position)
    • Collect a series of 5x30s ENGTEST images with the shutter open to measure ambient light conditions
    • Repeat this block for all filters currently installed in ComCam. 
  • Repeating these steps at a different azimuth position.
precondition: Dome is closed but telescope and dome motion are available. Mirror covers open.

name: Short-exposure donut stamps to understand scintillation effects
Observe the Eutelsat 117 W GPS WAAS satellite for timing test.
objective:
The Eutelsat 117 W satellite is used by the GPS system to relay measured GPS ground corrections to airplanes which use the information for precision landing etc. It is a geosynchronous satellite and is kept in the same location in the sky.

Unlike most satellites (whose public posted orbital parameters are only known on the km scale.  EUTSAT 117W should be known to cm.  The data is published here:

https://www.nstb.tc.faa.gov/RTData_WaasSatelliteData.htm

Eutelsat 117W is labeled as PRN 131 (the pseudo random # used for frequency modulation) on this page.  I  (CWW) have been scraping information from this page ever 3 minutes for some days now to understand where it is precisely located.  

The goal of this test is attempt to observe the satellite when it is brightest, which should be about 3:00am local time.  It is relatively low down on the horizon as it is located at 117W Earth Longitude.

We will observe by centering the ComCam field center at the average position over the week ending 11/20/24.

```
EUTELSAT_117W_B      AZ Min:295.699 Max: 295.727      Mean:295.713
EUTELSAT_117W_B      ALT Min:29.082 Max: 29.111      Mean:29.095
```

Based on a calculation using Stellarium the magnitude should be about 17 at 3:00 local time

```

23:00 19.10

24:00 18.23

01:00 17.59

02:00 17.17

03:00 17.02

04:00 17.44

05:00 17.41 -< phase angle 0

06:00 17.45

```

This data will be used to compare our measured position with that of the published positions to attempt to absolutely calibrate our timing.

The field is 40' on a side (.7 degrees or 2400").  The sky rotates at 15'/min so a 30 second exposure would be 7.5', a 10 second exposure 2.5' (or 750 pixels).  

So we will take both 5, and 10 second exposures.

name: Simonyi ComCam FBS SV Survey: Fornax Dwarf Spheroidal Galaxy
objective:
Observations for Science Pipelines Commissioning -- see Proposed strategy for Science Pipelines commissioning observations during late stages of ComCam on-sky campaign

Details

The objective of this test is to collect sequences of ComCam images for science pipelines commissioning.

The observations are implemented with the Feature Based Scheduler to allow running this test at any time that the system can achieve acceptable image quality for science pipelines testing (e.g., PSF FWHM < 2 arcsec).

This test case is intended to be run as part of a multi-night observing campaign, i.e., this test could be repeated on multiple nights.

The underlying scheduler configuration is expected to be updated to adjust the prioritization of target fields, constraints, dither pattern, exposure time, band selection, etc., based on the evolving system capabilities as we move through on-sky commissioning w/ ComCam.

The data will be used for multiple science pipeline commissioning tasks, including:
  • Solving and validating the camera distortion model, including tests of astrometric repeatability
  • Solving and validating the illumination correction, including tests of photometric repeatability
  • Test building deep coadds
  • Test building templates for difference imaging and running difference image analysis

Goal to accumulate epochs on many nights for routine testing of Prompt Processing and DIA in as many bands as possible
  • For example, 10 visits in each of the three loaded filters per epoch
  • General preference to observe in 3 bands per epoch, to enable as many different tests as possible
precondition:
Telescope tracking + optically focused and aligned for 30 second visits, w/ acceptable delivered image quality across the ComCam field of view.

Confidence that the system can maintain the performance above for at least 30 min to 1 hour, including focal plane scale dithers between visits and larger slews between fields.

name: LUTT-003 Elevation Look-Up Table with Hexapod and Mirror Bending Modes Closed-Loop
objective:
This Test Case uses a configurable BLOCK to sweep the telescope in elevation in a grid to check for elevation dependence on the LUT at a fixed azimuth. 
At every step we run the closed loop for 5 iterations.

This BLOCK is part ComCam AOS tests.
The data is used to check for elevation dependence on the look up tables. Analysis will be done offline.
At each azimuth and elevation position, it takes a triplet (intra/extra/infocus image sequence).

The test case is broken up into three steps to ease execution. The three steps do not need to all be scheduled/run back-to-back, they are largely independent.

A default filter to use is also provided, but any filter can be used to complete the test in the case that the r_03 filter is not installed.

Observing Condition Requirements:
No specific observation conditions are required. This can be run in cloudy and poor seeing conditions.

While running this block:
  • check the images. of donut-donut-focused : RubinTV
  • check donut pipe line running :  RubinTV donut pipeline check
  • check the hexapods moving : chronograf
precondition: CLT-001 has been completed and closed-loop is verified.<br id="isPasted">Optical state estimation has been verified.

name: glitch test, mirror raised, 50 deg elevation - 10% Settings GGRR
objective:
This tests is a diagnostic characterization Test that we want to perform to look at the torque glitches of the telescope we see that are affecting the other subsystems.
It will start with positioning the telescope pointing at 50º in elevation. We will use the full range of azimuth limits of the system (currently +/- 260).

In this version of the test case we want to run it with 10% setting applied with GGRR slew flags.

From there, this block will perform the following offsets:
  • move to -260 azimuth
  • move immediately to +260 azimuth
  • move immediately back to -260 azimuth
  • move immediately back to +260 azimuth

The GGRR suffix is associated with the Acceleration Forces, Balance Forces, Velocity Forces, Booster Valves. 
G means green and it means that both Acceleration Forces and Balance Forces should be enabled. 
R means red and it means that both Velocity Forces and Booster Valves should be disabled.
precondition:
• M1M3 must be enabled, raised, and with the force balance system active. 
  • M2 must be enabled and in closed-loop. 
  • MTMount should be controlled via CSC, enabled, and homed.
  • Proper TMA Motion Settings Applied

Note: For this test, we will use the maintel/move_p2p.py script.

name: ASCT-004 Sensitivity Camera Hexapod V2
objective:
Test Case Overview:
This test case involves re-running the parameter_march_comcam.py script, which systematically perturbs the dz degree of freedom (DoF) of the Camera Hexapod. The script adjusts the DoF through 6 incremental steps. At each increment, a triplet of exposures is captured using ComCam, with the camera rotator angle altered at each step.

Notes:
  • Each step in this test will produce 18 full-array ComCam exposures.
  • The collected data is essential for generating the sensitivity matrix, which maps the relationship between wavefront changes (measured via Zernike polynomials) and the actuation of each degree of freedom, whether through bending modes or rigid body motions.
Purpose:
The sensitivity matrix is crucial for understanding how adjustments in the Camera Hexapod’s degrees of freedom affect the wavefront. This knowledge is vital for fine-tuning the optical system to ensure optimal image quality.
precondition:
photometric conditions
optics aligned
filter agnostic
low to medium stellar density in the area
All CSCs for Simonyi telescope and ComCam should be enabled.

name: Dynamic Tests at El = 82º - short and long slews - 20% Settings GGGG
objective:
This tests is one of the many Dynamic Tests that we want to perform to evaluate if M1M3 and M2 can stand inertial forces when the telescope moves different velocity, acceleration, and jerk. It will start with positioning the telescope pointing at 82º in elevation. The initial azimuth position is not very relevant but it is set to -75º. However, there was no easy way to set it as a free parameter. So, if you need a new initial azimuth position, we will need to regenerate a new BLOCK JSON. 

In this version of the test case we want to run it with 20% setting applied.

From there, this block will perform the following offsets:
  • -12º offset in elevation
  • +12º offset in elevation
  • -3.5º offset in elevation
  • +3.5º offset in elevation
  • -24º offset in azimuth
  • +24º offset in azimuth
  • -3.5º offset in azimuth
  • +3.5º offset in azimuth

Long movements cause less stress (acceleration/de-acceleration) in the system. 
That is why they come first.

The GGRG suffix is associated with the Acceleration Forces, Balance Forces, Velocity Forces, Booster Valves. 
G means green and it means that both Acceleration Forces and Balance Forces should be enabled. 
R means red and it means that both Velocity Forces should be disabled.
precondition:
• M1M3 must be enabled, raised, and with the force balance system active. 
  • M2 must be enabled and in closed-loop. 
  • MTMount should be controlled via CSC, enabled, and homed.
  • Proper TMA Motion Settings Applied

Note: For this test, we will use the maintel/move_p2p.py script.

name: Closed Loop Truncation Test - coma modes
objective:
In this test, we change the truncation level in the closed loop configuration and run the closed loop to understand which modes need to be used.

We will see if we can enable the mirror bending modes associated with coma, and not get divergences in the closed loop.
- Use the closed loop to get into a good state
- Set truncation
- Run closed loop to ensure coma modes don't diverge
- If successful, add coma to the system and run closed loop again.

Primary Coma:
M1M3: B6, B7 (DOFs 15, 16)
M2: B6, B7 (DOFs 35, 36)

Secondary Coma:
M1M3: B15, B16 (DOFs 24, 25)
M2: B19, B20 (DOFs 48, 49)

name: CLT-001 Closed Loop Converge - Kick z11
objective:
Validate that the Optical Feedback Controller closed loop effectively converges to an optimal configuration when perturbed with a set of degrees of freedom (DOFs) and that it stabilizes to provide optimal image quality. The test will ensure that the system adjusts force actuators and rigid body motions dynamically, while monitoring the Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM) as the key metric for convergence.

Test scientists will evaluate the convergence rate and decide on necessary changes to the Optical Feedback Control (OFC) configuration. All system changes will be documented for traceability and future tests.

The test itself has only three steps, but they will be repeated multiple times, plus it will require the test scientists deciding on the following steps based on the data taken. The estimated time is 2h, but this is a rough estimate, it may take longer or shorter.
precondition:
- Wavefront estimation has been verified (WET-001)
- Telescope is aligned
- We are able to run in closed-loop, by taking images and applying corrections

objective:
This tests is one of the many Dynamic Tests that we want to perform to evaluate if M1M3 and M2 can stand inertial forces when the telescope moves different velocity, acceleration, and jerk. It will start with positioning the telescope pointing at 34º in elevation and -75º in azimuth. 

In this version of the test case we want to run it with Vel 40% Acc 40% Jerk 40%

From there, this block will perform the following offsets:

  • -12º offset in elevation
  • +3.5º offset in elevation
  • -3.5º offset in elevation
  • +24º offset in azimuth
  • -24º offset in azimuth
  • +3.5º offset in azimuth
  • -3.5º offset in azimuth

Long movements cause less stress (acceleration/de-acceleration) in the system.

See all versions in the Dynamic Tests Versions Confluence page.

The GGGG suffix is associated with the Acceleration Forces, Balance Forces, Velocity Forces, Booster Valves. 
G means green that a specific force is enabled. 
R means red that a specific force is disabled.

name: ASCT-004 Sensitivity Camera Hexapod
objective:
Test Case Overview:
This test case involves running BLOCK-T377, which systematically perturbs specific degrees of freedom (DoF) of the Camera Hexapod, one at a time, using the parameter_march_lsstcam.pyscript. The script adjusts each DoF through 9 incremental steps. At each increment, an in-focus is captured using LSSTCam, with the camera rotator angle altered at each step.

Notes:
  • The test should be completed in a single session to maintain consistency. 
  • If running the JSON BLOCK fails, each DoF should be perturbed individually by running parameter_march_lsstcam.py. Please, refer to the json block code to see the configurations.
  • Assuming 30-second exposures with a 5-second buffer per perturbation, each DoF requires 9*(30s + 5s) = 5.3min. The total test duration has been estimated based on this timing.
  • This test will produce 9 full-array LSSTCam exposures per degree of freedom.
  • The collected data is essential for generating the sensitivity matrix, which maps the relationship between wavefront changes (measured via Zernike polynomials) and the actuation of each degree of freedom, whether through bending modes or rigid body motions.

Purpose:
The sensitivity matrix is crucial for understanding how adjustments in the Hexapod’s degrees of freedom affect the wavefront. This knowledge is vital for fine-tuning the optical system to ensure optimal image quality.
precondition:
photometric conditions
optics aligned
filter agnostic
low to medium stellar density in the area
All CSCs for Simonyi telescope and ComCam should be enabled.

name: MTDome Mini-Cadence Test
objective:
During operations there are several requirements that the MTDome must meet:

  • Rotate from one position to another 3 degrees away within 4 seconds.

  • Be able to position the dome within 0.25 degrees from the target position.

  • Crawl the dome with velocities typically of about 0.1 to 0.4 degrees per second.

  • Be in constant motion and don't stop unless not otherwise possible.

  • Other requirements that are not relevant for this test.

Currently the MTDome does not meet the last requirement. It overshoots the target, stops and then moves back. This test focuses on the first three requirements.


This ​test is intended to record data into the EFD about the motion profile of the dome. The ​test operator should:
  • Abort the test in the event of any observed irregularity such as noise or test behavior inconsistent with the description
    • Verify that the EFD has recorded information in the `MTDome.azimuth` topic, including `positionActual`, `positionCommanded`, `velocityActual`, and `velocityCommanded`.

objective:
This Test Case uses a BLOCK to validate the wavefront estimation pipeline (WEP) using giant defocused objects (+/- 7.5mm). This BLOCK is part of the AOS tests for LSSTCam on sky. The data is used to compare the WEP for giant defocused objects (+/- 7.5mm) to regular defocused objects (+/- 1.5mm). Analysis will be done offline. This BLOCK will take two triplets of giant donuts with exposure time of 60 seconds and two standard exposures of in-focus objects with exposure time of 15 seconds. For a standard exposure, regular donuts will be provided by the wavefront sensors.

The test case is broken up into four steps to ease execution. The first step takes an RA and DEC to track, and the following three steps can be completed separately. This BLOCK is designed to run on whatever filter is already installed on LSSTCam. If possible, it should be run in more than one filter, but this would not need to be done consecutively. This BLOCK also does not need to be ran at three different zenith angles consecutively, so steps 2-4 of this test case can be treated separately.

objective: A common (but hopefully not repeated) condition that we met during EO testing was overexposure of the CCD’s, leading to high currents on sensors. This would routinely open the REB switches (tripping off !). The main thing that we’re concerned about while doing this test is whether or not right stars that will be frequent in the sky will trip off these REBs  during regular survey operations, either at the nominal survey cadence of approximately 30 seconds or the deep drilling field cadence.

name: LUTT-004 Azimuth Look-Up Table
objective:
This Test Case uses a configurable BLOCK to sweep the telescope in azimuth in a grid to check for azimuth dependence on the LUT at a fixed elevation. At every step we run the closed loop for one iteration (although you can override that value). The azimuths covered are np.arange(-180, 180, 30). The data is used to check for azimuth dependence on the look up tables. Analysis will be done offline. At each azimuth and elevation position, it takes an exposure.

The time estimate assumes two iterations of the closed loop at every iteration.

The test case is broken up into three steps to ease execution. The three steps do not need to all be scheduled/run back-to-back, they are largely independent.

A default filter to use is also provided, but any filter can be used to complete the test in the case that the r_57 filter is not installed.

Observing Condition Requirements:
No specific observation conditions are required. This can be run in cloudy and poor seeing conditions.

While running this block:
  • check the images. of donut-donut-focused : RubinTV
  • check donut pipe line running :  RubinTV donut pipeline check
  • check the hexapods moving : chronograf
precondition:
CLT-001 has been completed and closed-loop is verified.
Optical state estimation has been verified with WET-001 tests.

name: LUTT-011 Full Azimuth-Elevation-Rotator Look-Up Table
objective:
This Test Case uses a configurable BLOCK to sweep the telescope in elevation, azimuth, and rotator angle in a grid to check for dependencies on the LUT, sweeping through the parameter space.
The data is used to check for rotation dependence on the look up tables. Analysis will be done offline. At each point (elevation, azimuth, rotation angle) it takes an exposure.

The test case is broken up into three steps to ease execution. The three steps do not need to all be scheduled/run back-to-back, they are largely independent.

A default filter to use is also provided, but any filter can be used to complete the test in the case that the r_57 filter is not installed.

Observing Condition Requirements:
No specific observation conditions are required. This can be run in cloudy and poor seeing conditions.

While running this block:

name: Closed-dome Rotator Tracking Test
objective:
Perform closed-dome slew and tracking tests with the MTRotator. First, we need to test rotator performance at a different hour angles (which correspond to different tracking speeds). This can be accomplished using the track_target.py script.

If successful, we should then test rotator tracking performance for targets transiting near zenith with small offsets to simulate science observations. We will use a scheduler-driven survey with appropriate targets for the time-of-day and substitute the track_target_and_take_image.py block with a suitable replacement.

The scheduler should run for at least an hour to allow the target to rise and transit so that we explore the peak rotator velocity.

name: LSSTCam OFF-field stray light within a filter
objective:
This test collects the data for spotting potential stray light generated by a bright star outside the LSSTCam field of view, between angles 4.1° and X° off-axis.

There are different off-axis stray light patterns depending on the amplitude of the off-axis position:
  • 4.1°-5.9° FoV outskirt 
  • 6°-12° off-axis, M3 direct path of scattered through M3 direct path (dedicated test case)
  • 12°-17° off-axis, stray light from M2 baffle 
  • > 17° off-axis, stray light from dome 

This test procedure applies to one single LSSTCam filter; upon time availability, the test should be conducted through different filters. The Anti-Reflection coatings of the LSSTCam optics are more efficient than the ComCam coatings, therefore we use a very bright star as Alpha Centauri (mag_V = 1.33).

Note: the minimum LSSTCam exposure time is 1 sec, with a readout time of 2.8 sec.
precondition:
• The telescope system must be collimated and focused
  • The telescope must be tracking the target
  • AOS shall be in closed loop
  • I filter shall be engaged
  • LSSTCam needs to be enabled.

name: LSSTCam stray light from M2 baffle
objective: This test collects the data for spotting potential stray light generated by the M2 baffle for large off-axis angles with the LSSTCam. The M2 baffle is black anodized and we suspect it might create some stray light patterns for a bright off-axis star position between 14° and 19°. The M2 highest reflectance falls within the Z and Y bands.
precondition:
• The telescope system must be collimated and focused
  • The telescope must be tracking the target
  • LSSTCam needs to be enabled.

name: LSSTCam IN&OFF field stray light using CBP
objective:
This test collects the data for spotting potential stray light generated within the LSSTCam field of view (FoV) using the CBP (collimated beam projector) in daytime. The CBP projects a localized, collimated beam of about 1-meter diameter within the Rubin entrance pupil (M1) that it is used to materialize stray light paths (if any) within and outside the telescope FoV.
Note: the test shall be conducted with 1 mm pinhole mask within the CBP. 
Note: the absolute photometric calibration with an electrometer is not particularly important.

Test pseudo-sequence: 
  • Point the CBP wrt the TMA to make a relative angle X between the two systems
  • Turn on the CBP laser and set it  to the left-side wavelength of the filter where the filter transmission is about 50% (see table below), take an image
  • Switch the CBP laser to the central wavelength of the filter where the filter transmission is about 98% (see table below), take an image
  • Switch the CBP laser to the right-side wavelength of the filter where the filter transmission is about 50% (see table below), take an image
  • Change the CBP pointing wrt the TMA to another angle and repeat the previous steps
  • Explored field range 0° to 3° with steps of 0.2°.

name: LSSTCam IN-field stray light occulted star with different filters
objective:
This test collects the data for discerning the type of coating deposited on the LSSTCam filters. Having a filter coated on both surfaces with a bandpass window, or one surface coated with a bandpass and the other with an AR coating (anti-reflection), leads to different stray light/ghost patterns, as shown in the simulation below. The star is brought into the gap between two adjacent rafts or two adjacent detectors to mask the PSF and highlight the halo features.
The procedure shall be repeated for different filters since their coating deposition can be different.
Important note: please monitor the camera bias thresholds at this link: https://summit-lsp.lsst.codes/chronograf/sources/1/dashboards/558?refresh=10s&lower=now%28%29%20-%201h
Note: the space between rafts 500 microns is larger than the space between detectors (250 microns).
precondition:
• The telescope shall be collimated and in focus
  • A filter of the LSSTCam shall be engaged
  • LSSTCam shall be enabled.

name: Generic TMA Dynamic Test
objective:
This is a Generic TMA Dynamic Tests that we want to perform to evaluate if M1M3 and M2 can stand inertial forces when the telescope moves different velocity, acceleration, and jerk. 
It will start with positioning the telescope pointing at high (82º), mid (70º), or low (34º) elevations.​
The initial Azimuth position is not very relevant. It should be changed according best convenience. 

From the initial position, this block will perform the following sequence of single direction offsets:
  • +12º offset in elevation
  • -12º offset in elevation
  • +3.5º offset in elevation
  • -3.5º offset in elevation
  • +24º offset in azimuth
  • -24º offset in azimuth
  • +3.5º offset in azimuth
  • -3.5º offset in azimuth

Additionally, it will perform the following sequence of diagonal movements, which combine azimuth and elevation offsets.

Note 1: Long movements cause less stress (acceleration/de-acceleration) in the system. That is why they come first.
Note 2: See all versions in the Dynamic Tests Confluence page.
precondition:
• MTPtg must be enabled
  • M1M3 must be enabled, raised, and with the force balance system active. 
  • M2 must be enabled and in closed-loop. 
  • MTMount should be controlled via CSC, enabled, and homed.
  • Proper TMA Motion Settings Applied
  • Proper M1M3 Settings Applied

Note: For this test, the configurable block uses the short_long_slews.py to perform the offsets defined above.

name: TMA Dynamic Test at El = 70 - Vel 5% Acc 5% Jerk 5% - GGGR
objective:
This tests is one of the many Dynamic Tests that we want to perform to evaluate if M1M3 and M2 can stand inertial forces when the telescope moves different velocity, acceleration, and jerk. 
It will start with positioning the telescope pointing at 70º in elevation. 
The initial azimuth position is not very relevant.
It should be changed according best convenience. 

In this version of the test case we want to run it with Vel/Acc/Jerk 5%/5%/5% setting applied.

From there, this block will perform the following sequence of single directions offsets:
  • +12º offset in elevation
  • -12º offset in elevation
  • +3.5º offset in elevation
  • -3.5º offset in elevation
  • +24º offset in azimuth
  • -24º offset in azimuth
  • +3.5º offset in azimuth
  • -3.5º offset in azimuth

Additionally, there will diagonal movements which combine azimuth and elevation offsets.

Long movements cause less stress (acceleration/de-acceleration) in the system.

name: LSSTCam stray light from L3 chamfer - crowded field
objective:
This test collects data for confirming the stray light from the L3 chamfer (angel wings pattern) observed in the proximity of the four LSSTCam FoV corners (image below) within an annulus at 2°+/- 50" from the center of FoV. 


Optical simulations indicate that this stray light feature is generated by the L3 chamfer at the edge of the L3 clear aperture. To confirm this scenario and assess the angular extent of the field suffering this problem, the test shall place a dense stellar object at one of the corners of the LSSTCam FoV to maximize the number of stars affected by stray light angel wings pattern.

name: Characterize M1M3 Thermal System Mixing Valve
objective:
The coolant recirculation system is used to control the air plenum temperature and through this, the mirror temperature. The mixing valve is used to mix cold coolant from the chillers with coolant inside the cell lowering the temperature of the mirror cell recirculating coolant allowing the mirror temperature to follow the ambient temperature changes a couple of degrees below. The mixing valve controller will be a PID controller whose parameters will be obtained from characterizing the system and tuning. 

We will use the data to obtain the transfer function of the system. Mixing valve should be closed at the beginning of this test.
precondition: Make sure you have some support by someone who is familiar with the M1M3 thermal system and GUI.

name: LSSTCam Sequencer Test
objective:
This will test when a sequencer is updated. It will take biases, darks and a 500 pair PTC curve. 

If the network is unreliable or if there are power glitches, some of the hardware may fault or timeout: Electrometer:103, LinearStage:101, 102, 103, and LEDProjector.
If any of these go to fault, do the following:
  1. Stop the PTC curve and cycle the CSCs so that they are re-ENABLED.
  2. Take note of the most recent exposure time completed in the PTC sequence. 
  3. FInd the exposure time in the configuration file, found at `ts_observatory_control/data/mtcalsys.yaml`. The sequence name is `ptc_i_39_500`.
    1. Note that there will be some differences between the camera exposure time and the exposure time listed in teh configuration file. When an exposure time is listed (in the configuration file) as less than 1 second, it is actually at that value * 100 with a lower LED level. If the level is listed as higher than 30 seconds, it is actually that value - 40 seconds with a higher LED level.
  4. Edit the config file `mtcalsys.yaml` so that everything before the most recent exposure time is deleted. Push this change to the run branch of ts_observatory_control
  5. Start step 8 again
precondition:

name: LSST Sequence B+ Protocol
objective:
Test for new camera sequencer. It includes the following:

  • Set of 25 biases with 30s gap (for stability + reference bias).  Reason bias, duration 15 minutes.

  • Set of 25 darks (30s) (for stability + reference dark).  Reason dark, duration 15 minutes.

  • Set of 40 flats (10s) (for gain stability).  Reason gain_stability, duration 10 minutes.

  • Set of bias stability biases to test idle clear (or lack thereof).  This would be bias/30s/bias/60s/bias/120s/bias/180s/bias/240s/bias, and would take 10 minutes.

  • Persistence test: 60s flat at 0.8 illumination, followed by 5 30s darks, duration 5 minutes.

  • 100 pair PTC.  Looking at the timing of the other night this would take 90-95 minutes.

If it is used to test several sequencers at a time, it will look something like the following. You can just repeat Steps 5 and 6 in this test case.

  1. Install 3s_RT.seq

  2. run BLOCK-T546

  3. Install 3s_Paralle.seq

  4. run BLOCK-T546

  5. Install 3s_ISO2.seq

  6. run BLOCK-T546

Note: if the laser tracker is being difficult it is a "nice to have" but not required to have a successful run.
Note: the block will open and close the MTReflector

name: LSSTCam stray light - pillow - repeatability
objective:
This test attempts to reproduce the stray light pillow pattern that seems to be created by the Moonlight. The test needs to be timely, the observation shall replicate the same sky and telescope configuration of the previous epochs of scratched tape observations, i.e. same star field, same AltAz, rotator angle, exposure time, dome orientation and filter engaged.

The goal is to put the Moon at the same separation from the FoV and at the same offset position angle where the Pillow has been previously observed. 
Note: the telescope pointing direction shall fall between S and W before dawn time.
precondition:
• The telescope system must be collimated and focused
  • The telescope must be tracking the target
  • LSSTCam needs to be enabled.

name: Test Hexapod Movement During Exposures
objective: The goal is to investigate whether hexapod movement during exposures degrades image quality.
precondition:
This test must be done when we have good image quality on-sky. The delivered image quality should ideally be sub-arc second, although sub-1.2 arc second is probably okay.
This test does NOT need to be taken in photometric conditions.

objective: Goal: use the CBP to study non-linear crosstalk. Complete this in the i-band with hopefully exposure time < 30 seconds
precondition: CBP and TMA are properly co-pointing. Laser is on.

name: TMA Dynamic Test at El = 45 - Vel 5% Acc 5% Jerk 5% - RRRR
objective:
This tests is one of the many Dynamic Tests that we want to perform to evaluate if M1M3 and M2 can stand inertial forces when the telescope moves different velocity, acceleration, and jerk. 
It will start with positioning the telescope pointing at 45º in elevation. 
The initial azimuth position is not very relevant. 
It should be changed according best convenience. 

In this version of the test case we want to run it with Vel/Acc/Jerk 5% / 5% / 5% setting applied.

From there, this block will perform the following sequence of single directions offsets:
  • +12º offset in elevation
  • -12º offset in elevation
  • +3.5º offset in elevation
  • -3.5º offset in elevation
  • +24º offset in azimuth
  • -24º offset in azimuth
  • +3.5º offset in azimuth
  • -3.5º offset in azimuth

Additionally, there will diagonal movements which combine azimuth and elevation offsets.

Long movements cause less stress (acceleration/de-acceleration) in the system. 
That is why they come first.

See all versions in the Dynamic Tests Confluence page.

The RRRR suffix is associated with the Acceleration Forces, Balance Forces, Velocity Forces, Booster Valves, in this order.
G means green that the corresponding forces should be enabled.
R means red that the corresponding forces should be disabled.
precondition:
• MTPtg must be enabled
  • M1M3 must be enabled, raised, and with the force balance system active. 
  • M2 must be enabled and in closed-loop. 
  • MTMount should be controlled via CSC, enabled, and homed.
  • Proper TMA Motion Settings Applied

Note: For this test, the configurable block uses the short_long_slews.py to perform the offsets defined above.

name: LSSTCam stray light from M2 baffle using CBP - integrated z band 16° off-axis (no filter)
objective:
This test collects the data for spotting potential stray light, integrated in the z band, generated by the M2 baffle at 16 deg off-axis angle with the LSSTCam using the CBP (collimated beam projector). The CBP projects a localized, collimated beam of about 1-meter diameter within the Rubin entrance pupil (M1). The M2 baffle is black anodized, and we suspect it might create some stray light patterns for a bright off-axis star position between 12° and 20°. 
During the test laser wavelengths are scanned at steps of 10nm within the z filter bandwidth between 810 and 910 nm.

Note: the test shall be conducted with a 1 mm pinhole mask within the CBP.
Note: the absolute photometric calibration with electrometer would be needed to estimate the surface brightness of the M2 baffle halo.

Test pseudo-sequence: 
  • Point the CBP wrt the TMA to make a relative angle 16° between the two systems
  • Turn on the CBP laser 
  • Run BLOCK-T580 that switches the laser through the Z band wavelengths at steps of 10nm
precondition:
• NO filter in the LSSTCam shall be engaged
  • The telescope shall be collimated
  • The CBP shall be available
  • The 1 mm pinhole mask of the CBP shall be engaged
  • The dome lights shall be OFF.

name: LSSTCam stray light from LSSTCam filters shiny plate

name: LSSTCam HV Bias Safe Moon Separation Verification
objective:
The objective of this test is to test the currently defined moon separation limits (30 degrees for standard survey operations, suggested 20 degrees for camera safety) and the minimum separation we should define to ensure we do not trip the HV bias.

In order to map out the illumination pattern of stray light from the Moon, imaging around the Moon (possibly a region of 25x25 degrees) with HV off shall be executed. Whether the camera should include the Moon in the FoV needs discussion, but the camera team has experience shining the focal plane with a flashlight with HV off. We could also avoid the region a few degrees away from the Moon, just in case. We could start the separation between pointing of 3 degrees to shorten the execution time. If the test shows some interesting feature, we should detail those regions.

This observation can reveal the sky brightness as a function of the distance to the Moon, as well as the map of the sweet spot where the camera sees strong stray light, which will fall in the interest of the stray light group. 

Note that with HV off, the dynamic range will be lowered, and the gain could be different. The measurement will be relative.

This test has no filter preference. 1s exposures are sufficient.

name: TMA Dynamic Test at El = 70 - Vel 10% Acc 10% Jerk 10% - GGGG
objective:
This tests is one of the many Dynamic Tests that we want to perform to evaluate if M1M3 and M2 can stand inertial forces when the telescope moves different velocity, acceleration, and jerk. 
It will start with positioning the telescope pointing at 70º in elevation. 
The initial azimuth position is not very relevant. 
It should be changed according best convenience. 

In this version of the test case we want to run it with Vel/Acc/Jerk 10% / 10% / 10% setting applied.

From there, this block will perform the following sequence of single directions offsets:
  • +12º offset in elevation
  • -12º offset in elevation
  • +3.5º offset in elevation
  • -3.5º offset in elevation
  • +24º offset in azimuth
  • -24º offset in azimuth
  • +3.5º offset in azimuth
  • -3.5º offset in azimuth
Additionally, there will diagonal movements which combine azimuth and elevation offsets.

Long movements cause less stress (acceleration/de-acceleration) in the system. 
That is why they come first.

See all versions in the Dynamic Tests Confluence page.

The GGGG suffix is associated with the Acceleration Forces, Balance Forces, Velocity Forces, Booster Valves, in this order.
G means green that the corresponding forces should be enabled.
R means red that the corresponding forces should be disabled.
precondition:
• MTPtg must be enabled
  • M1M3 must be enabled, raised, and with the force balance system active. 
  • M2 must be enabled and in closed-loop. 
  • MTMount should be controlled via CSC, enabled, and homed.

name: TMA Dynamic Test at El = 70 - Vel 30% Acc 20% Jerk 20% - GGGG
objective:
This tests is one of the many Dynamic Tests that we want to perform to evaluate if M1M3 and M2 can stand inertial forces when the telescope moves different velocity, acceleration, and jerk. 
It will start with positioning the telescope pointing at 70º in elevation. 
The initial azimuth position is not very relevant. 
It should be changed according best convenience. 

In this version of the test case we want to run it with Vel/Acc/Jerk 30% / 20% / 20% setting applied.

From there, this block will perform the following sequence of single directions offsets:
  • +12º offset in elevation
  • -12º offset in elevation
  • +3.5º offset in elevation
  • -3.5º offset in elevation
  • +24º offset in azimuth
  • -24º offset in azimuth
  • +3.5º offset in azimuth
  • -3.5º offset in azimuth

Additionally, there will diagonal movements which combine azimuth and elevation offsets.

Long movements cause less stress (acceleration/de-acceleration) in the system. 
That is why they come first.

See all versions in the Dynamic Tests Confluence page.

The GGGG suffix is associated with the Acceleration Forces, Balance Forces, Velocity Forces, Booster Valves, in this order.
G means green that the corresponding forces should be enabled.
R means red that the corresponding forces should be disabled.
precondition:
• MTPtg must be enabled
  • M1M3 must be enabled, raised, and with the force balance system active. 
  • M2 must be enabled and in closed-loop. 
  • MTMount should be controlled via CSC, enabled, and homed.
  • Proper TMA Motion Settings Applied

Note: For this test, the configurable block uses the short_long_slews.py to perform the offsets defined above.

name: M2 closed-loop break-out brake test during TMA slew - 30% (velocity only) Settings GGGG
objective:
Proceed with caution - this is a test that might put lots of stress on M2. 
This is one of the gateway tests required to increate the TMA maximum velocity, acceleration, and jerk.

This test is originally defined in the LVV-T3034 test case. 
In summary, we want to know how M2 behaves when it goes out of closed loop in the middle of a slew. 

This test case is a bit different from the others. It will require two script queues and it has no JSON BLOCK. 
In one queue, we will send a command to move the telescope in Azimuth. Hopefully a very long slew.
Once the telescope starts moving, we will send a command to open the loop on M2 using another queue. 
MTMount, and maybe other components, will go to a fault. 

In this version of the test case we want to run it with 30% speed settings applied (NewSettings30percentspeed).

webLinks.description: LVV-T3034 - M2 closed-loop break-out during TMA slew - Gateway test

name: TMA Elevation Brake Distance - 30% speed Settings GGGG
objective:
We want to evaluate how much the telescope moves after engaging the brakes in Elevation. 
The only existing easy way to engage the brakes is to force the telescope to go to a fault state.
We will do that by using an access gate interlock which will trigger a hard stop fault on the TMA only.
This means that the telescope will start moving and it will fault while traveling at its maximum allowed velocity. 
This strategy allows us faulting the telescope without using more dramatic options, like an e-stop. 

In this version of the test case we want to run it with 30% speed setting applied.

The list of settings sets should be updated in the TMA Motion Settings page.
precondition:
• M1M3 must be enabled, raised, and with the force balance system active. 
  • M2 must be enabled and in closed-loop.

  • Proper TMA Motion Settings Applied

If there is an interruption, due to Fault or other issues, and you plan to continue this block;

  1. take note of the sequence number that appears in the "last checkpoint" field in the script. It will look something like this:

    Last checkpoint: [16/19]:: az=120.77, el=69.48, rot_seq=[60, 0, -60].

  3. Rerun the script passing: skip: <sequence number>.

If you need to stop the block to do some other activity and don't expect to immediately resume;

name: TMA Dynamic Test at El = 45 - Vel 5% Acc 5% Jerk 5% - GGGG
objective:

name: LSSTCam: vacuum stability verification under dynamic TMA loads
objective:
This test verifies that the camera maintains stable vacuum levels under dynamic operational conditions following recent vacuum sealing procedure.

Vacuum Monitoring: It must be monitored via the Cryo Vacuum Dashboard.

The test consists of executing a series of TMA and subsystem movements to verify that the camera can hold the current vacuum levels.
All initial movements are to be executed at 5% velocity to ensure safety and stability. 
The following movements should be executed. Small bumps in pressure are expected. Stop if a positive slope in pressure appears:

  1. Rotate carousel 5 times (only camera team can do this step, plans exist for them to do this early, skip if camera team not available, filter change is appox equivalent)
  2. Change filter 2 times
  3. Rotate camera rotator +/- 10 degrees 2 times
  4. Rotate camera rotator +/- 30 degrees 2 times
  5. Rotate camera rotator +/- 50 degrees 2 times
  6. TMA azimuth +10 degrees
  7. TMA azimuth -20 degrees
  8. TMA azimuth +30, -40, +50, -60, +70
  9. Elevation +10 (from horizon), then to +30, +60, zenith

Upon successful completion of the above, run dynamic tests with 5%,10% and 20%. 
Note: Kevin R. sign should sign off before we to increase speed to 10% and 20%.

Secondary Verification Goal:
- Confirm nominal TMA movement following the Azimuth replacement (OBS-1560).
- Confirm that the EPTB + El+ alarm (OBS-350) does not trigger during elevation or azimuth maneuvers.
precondition:

name: Simonyi LSSTCam Feature Based Scheduler Science Verification Field Survey
objective:
The objective of this test is to collect sequences of LSSTCam images for early Science Pipelines commissioning and observations of specific astronomical targets. Each of the observation sequences consists of dithered visits around a pointing center.

The observations are implemented with the Feature Based Scheduler to allow running this test at any time that the system can achieve acceptable image quality for Science Pipelines testing (e.g., PSF FWHM < 2 arcsec).

This test case is intended to be run as part of a multi-night observing campaign, i.e., this test could be repeated on multiple nights.

The data will be used for multiple Science Pipeline commissioning tasks, including:
  • Solving and validating the camera distortion model, including tests of astrometric repeatability
  • Solving and validating the illumination correction, including tests of photometric repeatability
  • Test building deep coadds
  • Test building templates for difference imaging and running difference image analysis

Note: Goal to accumulate epochs on many nights for routine testing of Prompt Processing and DIA in as many bands as possible
precondition:
Telescope tracking + optically focused and aligned for 30 second visits, w/ acceptable delivered image quality across the LSSTCam field of view.

Confidence that the system can maintain the performance above for at least 30 min, including focal plane scale dithers between visits, as well as larger slews between fields.
