name: ASCT-004 Sensitivity M2 Bending
objective:
Test Case Overview:
This test case involves running BLOCK-T379, which systematically perturbs specific degrees of freedom (DoF) of the M2 Bending Modes, one at a time, using the parameter_march_lsstcam.py script. The script adjusts each DoF through 9 incremental steps. At each increment, an in-focus is captured using LSSTCam, with the camera rotator angle altered at each step.

Notes:
  • The test should be completed in a single session to maintain consistency. 
  • If running the JSON BLOCK fails, each DoF should be perturbed individually by running parameter_march_lsstcam.py. Please, refer to the json block code to see the configurations.
  • Assuming 30-second exposures with a 5-second buffer per perturbation, each DoF requires 9*(30s + 5s) = 5.3min. The total test duration has been estimated based on this timing.
  • This test will produce 9 full-array LSSTCam exposures per degree of freedom.
  • The collected data is essential for generating the sensitivity matrix, which maps the relationship between wavefront changes (measured via Zernike polynomials) and the actuation of each degree of freedom, whether through bending modes or rigid body motions.

Purpose:
The sensitivity matrix is crucial for understanding how adjustments in the bending modes degrees of freedom affect the wavefront. This knowledge is vital for fine-tuning the optical system to ensure optimal image quality.

optics aligned
filter agnostic

name: Collect information about hexapod idle feature
objective:
We have had some recurring issues with the hexapod "idle" feature, that we have not been able to identify the cause to. Basically, the hexapods have this feature that if they are idle for more than a configurable amount of time, they will put the controllers in Standby. They are supposed to wake up the controllers if a move command happens or if there is a compensation correction. However, what we normally see is that the hexapod do not wake up expected, at least not in the case where there is a compensation correction.

This test case is designed to collect some information about this issue so we can investigate it. It consists of allowing the Hexapods to idle, then move the telescope by a few degrees in elevation to force a compensation correction and monitoring what happens.
precondition:
The main pre-condition for running this test is that we are able to move the mount and have the hexapods in Enabled/compensation enabled.

Other than that it can be executed anytime during the day or night, if we are closed down due to weather.

name: FBS-driven closed loop stability test - PID Gain Optimization (kp)
objective:

We will use the AOS closed-loop stability test to evaluate the convergence and stability of delivered image quality for different PID gain settings.

It uses the FBS to drive an AOS closed loop stability test using the MTAOS closed loop task. The telescope pointing (elevation, azimuth, rotator angle, filter) will remain fixed.

Test Approach:

  • The proportional gain (Kp) will be varied, with Ki and Kd set to zero.

  • The scheduler will run for 1 hour at each Kp value:

    • Kp = 0.05, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 0.45

    • For each point in the Kp grid, a summit support scientist should configure the MTAOS accordingly before the fbs scheduler is resumed. 

Next Steps:

  • Once the optimal Kp value is identified, the test will be extended to include a grid search over Ki and Kd values, further optimizing the PID controller for the MTAOS system.

name: Wavefront Retrieval Independence from Donut Size: Quintuplet Camera Defocus Sequence - 2 Rotator Angles
objective:
Goal: Verify that wavefront estimation is independent of donut size by comparing FAM measurements taken at two defocus levels (±0.5mm and ±1.5mm) across two camera rotator positions. This test investigates whether filter and/or L3 lens effects introduce systematic biases in wavefront retrieval that depend on the defocus amplitude.

Description:
The corner wavefront sensors derive Zernike coefficients from defocused donut images. The standard FAM observation uses ±1.5mm defocus, producing large donuts. There is a concern that the filter and L3 lens assembly may introduce non-uniform background or vignetting effects that depend on donut size, potentially biasing the wavefront solution. By comparing results at ±0.5mm (small donuts) and ±1.5mm (large donuts) at the same telescope state, we can determine whether the retrieved wavefront is consistent across donut sizes. Two rotator angles (0° and 60°) are used to separate camera-fixed patterns (e.g., filter/L3 effects that rotate with the camera) from sky-fixed patterns (e.g., astigmatism from optics alignment).

Test execution:

This test takes 10 quintuplets at each of two rotator angles (0° and 60°), producing 100 total exposures. Each quintuplet consists of 5 images at camera hexapod dZ positions [-1500, -500, 0, +500, +1500] µm, covering two donut sizes (small at ±500 µm and large at ±1500 µm) plus an in-focus image.

name: AOS Alternating-Elevation Stability - Open Loop Full Array Mode
objective:
Goal: Assess the stability and consistency of the optical differential between two elevation coordinates to inform lookup table development. By alternating FAM triplets between elevation 70° and 40° in rapid succession, the test isolates the true elevation-dependent optical changes from common-mode time variability (atmosphere, thermal drift).

The telescope optics change with elevation due to gravity-induced deformations. Characterizing these changes is essential for building lookup tables that pre-compensate for elevation-dependent aberrations. However, time-varying effects (atmospheric turbulence, thermal evolution) can confound the measurement if the two elevations are observed sequentially. By interleaving triplets — taking one at el=70°, then immediately slewing to el=40° for another, and repeating — the time-varying component should affect both elevations equally within each pair. Differencing the paired measurements cancels the common-mode drift, isolating the true elevation-dependent optical signal. This test is performed in open loop (no corrections applied) to observe the raw optical state at each elevation. It is designed to isolate the true differential by removing common-mode time variability.

Estimated duration: ~30-40 minutes (excluding initial alignment).

name: AOS Alternating-Rotator Stability - Open Loop Full Array Mode
objective:
Goal: Assess the stability and consistency of the optical differential between two rotator angles to inform lookup table development. By alternating FAM triplets between rotator angles (0° and 60°) in rapid succession while keeping elevation fixed, the test isolates the true rotator-dependent optical changes from common-mode time variability (atmosphere, thermal drift).

This is the rotator-alternating version of BLOCK-T720 (AOS Alternating-Elevation Stability - Open Loop FAM), which alternates between elevation. Here, instead, we keep az/el (El=70) and alternates rotator angles between one and other triplets sequence.

name: Dome Handover Procedure
objective:
Ensuring the dome is ready for night time observations.

Procedure Overview
The majority of this procedure is expected to be carried out by the daytime engineering team. It usually starts around 3:30pm CLT. Points of contact for the handover procedures are Juan Fabrega, Luis Vergara, Hernán Herrera, and Eduardo Serrano. The walkaround consists of carefully walking the dome floor and ensuring it is clear for movement. The daycrew will then check the dome controller and configure it for remote control. Then, we must perform a test that we can successfully move the dome components (azimuth, shutter, louvers) remotely via CSC. If that test succeeds, the handover is complete. 

The electrical team will initially move the dome manually to 328 deg and switch dome control to remote mote. When they do it, the brakes will be engaged. At this point, the dome is handed to us so we can take CSC control of it.
precondition:
1. Make sure laptops are configured and pre-loaded with the tools needed for the handover before going to L7. Be ready before hand. This is extremely important to avoid delaying the process. 
  2. The M1M3 mirror cover must be closed (deployed) before moving the dome shutter. If the TMA is parked at the horizon or calibration position, and it has been visually confirmed that the dome is clear and the shutter was previously tested to be free of ice/water (after a storm/rain event), it is acceptable to open the shutter slightly even if the mirror cover is not deployed.. 
  3. The electrical team should deliver the dome at 328 deg. If operation in Full Performance, the capacitor banks should be connected. Electrical team should make sure they are. Also dome crane lights should be off.
  4. Make sure that you read guidelines for the Dome in the Temporary Guidelines - LSSTCam On-Sky. 
  5. Need to have access to main-brick01.cp.lsst.org Windows 10 VM (https://ls.st/main-brick01).

name: Verify MTHexapod idle feature
objective:
The MTHexapod (Cam and M2 Hexapods) CSCs have a feature to disable the actuator drivers if the hexapod is idle (not moving) for a configurable amount of time. 
Up until version v1.8.4 (released in 2026-04-30), this feature was not working correctly which essentially prompted us to disable it by setting extremely large idle times in the MTHexapod configuration.

At the same time, we have never verified that, as required, the hexapods retain their position when the drivers are idled and, when idle, remain in position during tracking. 
This test is designed to test this feature such that we can configure it to power down the drivers during exposures.

name: ASCT-004 Sensitivity M1M3 Bending
objective:
Test Case Overview:
This test case involves running BLOCK-T378, which systematically perturbs specific degrees of freedom (DoF) of the M1M3 Bending Modes, one at a time, using the parameter_march_lsstcam.pyscript. The script adjusts each DoF through 9 incremental steps. At each increment, an in-focus is captured using LSSTCam, with the camera rotator angle altered at each step.

Notes:
  • The test should be completed in a single session to maintain consistency. 
  • If running the JSON BLOCK fails, each DoF should be perturbed individually by running parameter_march_lsstcam.py. Please, refer to the json block code to see the configurations.
  • Assuming 30-second exposures with a 5-second buffer per perturbation, each DoF requires 9*(30s + 5s) = 5.3min. The total test duration has been estimated based on this timing.
  • This test will produce 9 full-array LSSTCam exposures per degree of freedom.
  • The collected data is essential for generating the sensitivity matrix, which maps the relationship between wavefront changes (measured via Zernike polynomials) and the actuation of each degree of freedom, whether through bending modes or rigid body motions.

Purpose:
The sensitivity matrix is crucial for understanding how adjustments in the bending modes degrees of freedom affect the wavefront. This knowledge is vital for fine-tuning the optical system to ensure optimal image quality.

photometric conditions
optics aligned
filter agnostic
low to medium stellar density in the area

name: Warm-up Camera Hexapod
objective:
Warm up the grease inside the Camera Hexapod struts and lubricate part of the hardware. 

The warmup_hexapod.py script warms up hexapods by moving it to its maximum and minimum positions in discrete steps, using adaptive step sizes that adjust based on the success or failure of each movement to ensure smoother operation. It includes a verification phase to confirm the hexapod is properly warmed up, handling errors and faults during the process, with a maximum of 5 iterations to attempt the warm-up.

DON'T FORGET TO KEEP THE HEXAPOD DISABLED IF NOT GOING TO BE USED IN THE NEXT HOUR.
precondition:
• The MTHexapod:1 CSC should be in an ENABLED state.
  • Compensation mode should be disabled (the block does it internally, so no need to do it manually).
  • The Scheduler needs to be enabled too since we are using add_block.py script.
  • This test case can run in parallel CO2 Mirror Cleaning.
  • This test case cannot run in parallel with Mirror Reflectivity Measurements.

objective: Investigate whether air turbulence inside the dome exacerbates oil spreading on the TMA by performing a series of large azimuth slews (>100°) while the dome is in an open configuration. The test is executed using individual script-commanded slews (not scheduler-driven) to allow for controlled start/stop during the procedure. Mechanical team members will be present near the TMA during the run. Duration is approximately 3 hours (18:00–21:00 local), executable on a weekday afternoon or weekend with Freddy's team present.

  • Mechanical team (Freddy + ~3 members) must be present on-site
  • TMA operator must be stationed on L8, commanding from there (not the control room)
  • E-stops must be verified accessible on the TMA prior to the run
